title: Cluster 02 DRILL: Cell and Nuclear Division
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 3 · 10 questions · 113 marks · 45 parts · one mark per minute, so a little under two hours · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question. If you cannot trace a question to a paper, it is not in here.

Ten questions, 113 marks, 45 parts. The set is sized for coverage, not for the clock. Every learning outcome this cluster owns is tested more than once, from a different angle each time, because this is your first pass over the material. Questions 1 to 4 are mitosis, the cell cycle and chromosome structure, 49 marks; questions 5 to 10 are meiosis, significance and synthesis, 64 marks. Two sittings is the intended way to run it.

The anchors. Question 2 is the whole of 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 6, all four parts, at its real 11 marks. Question 7 is your own school's 2024 Paper 3 Section B essay at its real 10 marks. Question 5(a) is 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 17 and Question 5(c) is 9477 Specimen Paper 3 Question 1(b)(i) at its real 4 marks.

Six real figures, four questions figure-led. Chapter 3.2 is the most graph-driven chapter in Book 3 at 44.1% figure-led, and data and figure interpretation is 33.5% of Book 3 as a whole. Every figure is the real image from the paper the question came from, not a redrawing.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. The paper awards one mark for the letter. The drill then asks you to explain your answer, which is where you have to say whether every option is right and why. That follow-on wording is itself lifted from real papers that set it.

Cumulative, and that is the point. Q3(e) needs the growth factor, the receptor and the phosphorylation cascade said cold from Cluster 1. Q4(c) needs non-disjunction applied at anaphase I and at anaphase II. Q4(d) needs the three-level packing ladder from Book 2. Q5(f) needs unequal crossing over. Q8(c) needs polyploidy held apart from aneuploidy. Q9 needs semi-conservative replication in S phase. A Book 1 or Book 2 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 2 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Name the exact stage at which each event happens; the examiner report attached to Question 7 calls vague-across-stages description the commonest failure. Write non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes in full. State both sides of every comparison positively. Keep the centromere dividing apart from the kinetochore microtubules shortening. Quote figures off any graph you are told to refer to.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as duplicated labels. Q1 identifying mitotic stages from what is actually visible · Q2 reading a stage off quantitative spindle movement data · Q3 the cell cycle read from DNA content, and what controls its rate · Q4 the non-coding DNA at the ends and the middle of a chromosome · Q5 which events of meiosis generate variation, at precision level · Q6 the ploidy bookkeeping through both divisions, and why the number halves · Q7 the whole of cell division argued two ways at once · Q8 the spindle stage by stage, and what happens when it fails · Q9 counting chromosomes against counting DNA molecules · Q10 what each kind of division is for. Where an outcome is touched twice the two questions need different paragraphs of recall, not the same one. The single shared marking point in the set is crossing over at chiasmata, which Q5(c) needs alongside independent assortment and Q10(c) needs alongside random fertilisation; the stem of Q10(c) rules independent assortment out by name, so the two answers do not collapse into each other.

Nothing from Books 4 to 9, and nothing from Book 3 chapter 3.4. Stem cells and cancer are Cluster 3, so no question here needs them. Cyclin, CDK, MPF, karyotype, telomerase and the prophase sub-divisions are out of scope; the only mention of cyclins anywhere is a note in the Q3(e) answer saying the original key names them and that you do not need to.
